after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)=⟨t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.$
after.worked_solution:
Let $T(t)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the parameter $t.$ Since we are given the curve $r(t)$ parametrized by the parameter $t$ (not the arc length $s$), we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the corresponding unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,\operatorname{cos}⁡t,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨0,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}})}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where:

$$
r(s)=⟨\frac{3s+1}{5},\,\frac{3-4s}{5}⟩,\,s\ge 0
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{3s+1}{5}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{3-4s}{5})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{5},\,-\frac{4}{5}⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{3}{5}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\frac{4}{5})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{(0)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)$ given that its derivative ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$ are as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=⟨\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{{e}^{t}},\,-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{{e}^{t}}⟩,\,{T}^{′}(t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \sqrt{2({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \sqrt{2} \\  & =1 \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{{e}^{t}})}^{2}+{(-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{{e}^{t}})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡t-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t}{{e}^{2t}}+\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t}{{e}^{2t}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{t}}\cdot \sqrt{2({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{{e}^{t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the curvature is

$$

content.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)$ given that its derivative ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$ are as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=⟨\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{{e}^{t}},\,-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{{e}^{t}}⟩,\,{T}^{′}(t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \sqrt{2({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \sqrt{2} \\  & =1 \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{{e}^{t}})}^{2}+{(-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{{e}^{t}})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡t-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t}{{e}^{2t}}+\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t}{{e}^{2t}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{t}}\cdot \sqrt{2({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{{e}^{t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{{e}^{t}})} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡s)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡s,\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡s⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡s)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡s,\,0,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡s⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡s)}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{(-\operatorname{cos}⁡s)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡s+{cos}^{2}⁡s} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$
r(s)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡s,\,1,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡s⟩,\,0\le s<2\pi .
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡s)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡s,\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡s⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡s)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡s,\,0,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡s⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡s)}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{(-\operatorname{cos}⁡s)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡s+{cos}^{2}⁡s} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate r′(s) and r″(s): r′(s)=22⟨dds(s),dds(−cos⁡s),dds(sin⁡s)⟩=22⟨1,sin⁡s,cos⁡s⟩r″(s)=22⟨dds(1),dds(sin⁡s),dds(cos⁡s)⟩=22⟨0,cos⁡s,−sin⁡s⟩

Finally, the curvature is κ(s)=‖r″(s)‖=22⋅02+(cos⁡s)2+(−sin⁡s)2=22⋅cos2⁡s+sin2⁡s=22.
